# Proverbs 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** My-son, keep my-words, and-my-commandments treasure with-you.

**2** Keep my-commandments and-live, and-my-teaching like-[the]-apple-of your-eyes.

**3** Bind-them upon your-fingers; write-them upon [the]-tablet-of your-heart.

**4** Say to-wisdom, 'You [are] my-sister,' and-understanding call 'kinswoman,'

**5** To-keep-you from-[the]-strange woman, from-[the]-foreign-woman [who] makes-smooth her-words.

**6** For at-[the]-window-of my-house, through my-lattice I-looked-down,

**7** And-I-saw among-the-simple-ones, I-discerned among-the-youths a-young-man lacking heart,

**8** Passing in-the-street near her-corner, and-[the]-way-to her-house he-steps,

**9** In-twilight, in-[the]-evening-of [the]-day, in-[the]-pupil-of night and-darkness.

**10** And-behold, a-woman to-meet-him, [with]-dress-of a-prostitute and-guarded-of heart.

**11** Boisterous she [is] and-rebellious; in-her-house do-not-stay her-feet.

**12** Now in-the-street, now in-the-plazas, and-beside every corner she-lurks.

**13** And-she-seizes him and-kisses him; she-hardens her-face and-says to-him,

**14** "Sacrifices-of peace-offerings [are] upon-me; today I-have-fulfilled my-vows.

**15** Therefore I-have-come-out to-meet-you, to-seek your-face, and-I-have-found-you.

**16** With-coverings I-have-spread my-couch, colored-linens-of [the]-yarn-of Egypt.

**17** I-have-sprinkled my-bed [with]-myrrh, aloes, and-cinnamon.

**18** Come, let-us-drink-our-fill-of loves until the-morning; let-us-delight-ourselves with-caresses.

**19** For the-man [is]-not in-his-house; he-has-gone on-a-journey afar.

**20** The-bag-of money he-took in-his-hand; at-[the]-day-of the-full-moon he-will-come to-his-house."

**21** She-turns-him with-[the]-abundance-of her-persuasion; with-[the]-smoothness-of her-lips she-drives-him-away.

**22** He-goes after-her suddenly, like-an-ox to the-slaughter he-goes, and-like-a-fetter to-[the]-discipline-of a-fool,

**23** Until an-arrow splits his-liver — like-a-bird hastens to the-snare, and-does-not-know that for-his-life it [is].

**24** And-now, sons, hear to-me, and-attend to-[the]-words-of my-mouth.

**25** Let-not-turn your-heart to her-ways; do-not-wander in-her-paths.

**26** For many [are the]-slain she-has-felled, and-numerous [are] all her-killed-ones.

**27** Ways-of Sheol [is] her-house, going-down to chambers-of death.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **7:2**: Ishon (apple/pupil of the eye) — the most protected, sensitive part. Idiom for something guarded with utmost care.

- **7:14**: Shelamim (peace offerings) — the only sacrifice where the worshiper eats a portion. She uses religious duty as a pretext for the feast.

- **7:22-23**: Difficult text. 'Like a fetter to the discipline of a fool' — some emend to 'like a stag' (ayal for ekes). The liver-arrow image comes from hunting.

— EMET
